stem: In a decision tree, what does a leaf node hold?

options.text: The prediction: a class or a number

explanation: Internal nodes test features; leaves give the prediction.
source: General knowledge (topics asked in the 2023/24 CSC 572 paper, Questions 2 and 3)

stem: What is the entropy of a node that holds two classes in a 50/50 split?
explanation: H = −(0.5 log₂ 0.5 + 0.5 log₂ 0.5) = 1; a pure node has entropy 0.
source: General knowledge (topics asked in the 2023/24 CSC 572 paper, Questions 2 and 3)

stem: Which are pre-pruning (early stopping) limits for a decision tree?

options.text: Minimum samples to split a node
Cost-complexity pruning after the tree is grown

explanation: Cost-complexity pruning is post-pruning: the full tree is grown first, then cut back.
source: General knowledge (topics asked in the 2023/24 CSC 572 paper, Questions 2 and 3)

stem: A very deep tree that fits the training data almost perfectly but does badly on new data is overfitting.
explanation: Deep trees have low bias but high variance.
source: General knowledge (topics asked in the 2023/24 CSC 572 paper, Questions 2 and 3)

stem: How does a random forest combine its trees for a classification task?

options.text: It keeps only the deepest tree

explanation: Classification uses a vote; regression averages the trees' predictions.
source: General knowledge (topics asked in the 2023/24 CSC 572 paper, Questions 2 and 3)

stem: Which one is not part of how a random forest builds diverse trees?

options.text: Bootstrap samples of the training data
A random subset of features at each split
Scaling every feature to the range 0 to 1

explanation: Trees need no feature scaling; bagging plus feature randomness makes the trees differ.
source: General knowledge (topics asked in the 2023/24 CSC 572 paper, Questions 2 and 3)

stem: Adding more trees to a random forest always causes overfitting.
explanation: More trees make predictions more stable without overfitting, but the gains level off and the cost rises.
source: General knowledge (topics asked in the 2023/24 CSC 572 paper, Questions 2 and 3)

stem: Why does a random forest usually need no pruning?

options.text: Averaging many varied trees reduces the variance that deep trees have

explanation: Each tree has low bias and high variance; averaging lowers the variance.
source: General knowledge (topics asked in the 2023/24 CSC 572 paper, Questions 2 and 3)
